extracted.intended_audience: undergraduate students and instructors studying rhetorical/speech analysis; general readers interested in critiquing commencement speeches
extracted.subtask_description: Analyze a commencement speech (here, Conan O'Brien's Dartmouth 2011 address) for rhetorical effectiveness, focusing on appeals, tone, themes, and audience appropriateness. Produce a short critical essay assessing how devices (anecdotes, humor, references) serve the speech's purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of pathos (emotional appeal)
rubrics_metrics.description: The speaker 'appealed mostly to pathos ... He used pathos to appeal to the graduating students by telling about his falling out with NBC and how he came back to fame with his talk show on TBS.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the speaker uses personal stories of struggle, failure, and success to evoke emotions and connect with the audience. Example quote: 'I am here to tell you that whatever you think your dream is now, it will probably change. And that's okay.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of ethos (credibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: The speaker 'builds his credibility' through 'the use of his own personal stories about failure, and the references to other comedians.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate how personal experience and references to relevant peers/figures establish the speaker's authority and trustworthiness with the audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate balance of rhetorical appeals (minimize logos)
rubrics_metrics.description: Because this was a commencement speech, 'there wasn’t very much need to appeal to logos using stats or facts.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge whether the speech appropriately favors ethos/pathos over logos for the occasion; note if attempts at factual/logical appeals would feel out of place or unnecessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone and humor balance (keep it light-hearted)
rubrics_metrics.description: Even throughout serious personal stories, 'he would still sometimes slip in a humorous line to keep it light hearted and not too gloomy, which a commencement speech should all but not be.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check that humor is interspersed to prevent gloom, maintaining a light tone appropriate for graduation while not undermining the message.

rubrics_metrics.name: Central theme selection (failure and reinvention)
rubrics_metrics.description: The speech centers on failure as a theme: 'It is our failure to become our perceived ideal that ultimately defines us ... perceived failure can become a catalyst for profound re-invention.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess clarity and development of the central theme (here, failure/reinvention) and how effectively it delivers an inspirational message to the audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of personal anecdotes to illustrate points
rubrics_metrics.description: He tells about 'his falling out with NBC and how he came back to fame' as concrete anecdotes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate how well anecdotes illustrate the speaker's claims, create emotional resonance, and make abstract themes concrete for listeners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of references/examples (other comedians, role models)
rubrics_metrics.description: He references 'other comedians' and how 'great comedians have strived to be like the comedians they looked up to,' using these references to make a broader point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine whether intertextual references and examples help generalize the speaker's message, situate it in a tradition, or enhance credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience appropriateness and purpose clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: The speech is 'congratulating the graduating class and imparting a few words of wisdom.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge whether content, tone, rhetorical strategies, and examples are tailored to the graduating students and the occasion (celebratory, advisory), and whether the speech's purpose is clear and fulfilled.
